trans-unit.source: Technical backend user for vault access: UID of a backend user the asynchronous job runs as. Jobs execute in a Symfony Messenger consumer or on the CLI, where TYPO3 boots an unauthenticated command-line user - nr_vault then has no actor to authorise and denies every secret read, so the provider connection fails before any artifact is generated. Leave at 0 to keep the previous behaviour.
Pages per PDF: a PDF source with more pages fails before its pages are read with OCR or the layout reader, so one job cannot run an unbounded number of poppler and Vision calls. 200 if empty or 0.

Visible AI label on images: Renders a small "AI-generated" label (in the artifact's language) into the corner of every Schaubild HTML render and story slide. The full AI image (Schaubild ki_image) never passes the HTML renderer and carries the machine-readable marker only. The machine-readable markers in every file and in the artifact metadata are always written, whatever this setting says.

AI closing line on texts: Appends "This text was created with AI." (in the text's language) to the copy-ready text of the executive summary, FAQ, social posts and newsletter. Off by default: editors often paste these texts into places that carry their own AI disclosure, where a second one is noise. The social posts reserve the line's length inside their platform limit.

Webhook for social posts: Approved social posts are sent here by HTTP POST as JSON (platform, text, publishAt, sourceUrl, aiGenerated, aiLabel) when their time has come - run the command nr_repurpose:publish-due from the scheduler or cron. A scheduling tool, an automation service or an own endpoint puts them on the network. Empty: nothing is sent, and the command reports the posts that are due.

Webhook signing secret: With a secret, every request carries the header X-Nr-Repurpose-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body with this secret>, so the receiver can check that the post comes from this installation.
